name: K-Board Pro 4
summary: Dedicated family entry preserved for future editor routing and firmware mapping.

notes: Discovered 2026-08-16: under WinMM the whole device enumerates as a single "K-Board Pro 4" port pair (matched by the application profile's single_port style below), but under WMS the same physical device splits into two separately-named endpoints, "K-Board Pro 4 Control Surface" and "K-Board Pro 4 Expander" - found when --fw-update KBP4 under --midi-backend wms never located the device at all (WinMM's plain name never matched WMS's suffixed names). See the named_application profile below, added the same day following qunexus.json's identical legacy_unnamed_application/named_application split. Purpose of the Expander endpoint itself is unconfirmed - named by analogy with QuNexus's control_surface/expander/cv split, excluded from probing here out of the same caution, not a confirmed behavioral requirement.

Central's BOOTLOADER replies to a standard Universal Non-Realtime Device Inquiry (F0 7E 7F 06 01 F7) with a real Identity Reply (06 02) - handled generically by kmiDevice::midiCppIDReplyCallback(). Central's APPLICATION firmware detects the same inquiry (MIDI_sysex.c's sx_process(), CORE_SX_HEADER case) but replies with a KMI-proprietary "editor message" instead (SYX_FORMAT_KBP4_EDITOR_MESSAGE / SYX_FIRMWARE_VERSION_MSG=16, built by preset_sysex.c's send_firmware_version()) - found 2026-08-17 when --id-request kbp4 timed out every time in application mode despite working immediately in bootloader mode. kmiDevice::midiCppHostMessageCallback() (added the same day) parses this second reply format directly from the raw RX buffer (offsets documented in that function) and populates the same bootloaderVersion/applicationVersion fields - CONFIRMED on real hardware, both --midi-backend winmm and wms, reporting Bootloader version: 1.3.0 / Application version: 1.2.2 after a --fw-update KBP4 run, which is what first let us verify a flashed v1.2.2.0 image had actually landed and booted (the app only self-reports into the shared boot-status page after successfully running checkBootByte()/writeBootByte(), so a correct readback here is real evidence of a good flash, not just a SysEx transfer with no reported error). This reply carries no manufacturer/product/family ID fields, unlike the bootloader's real Identity Reply.

Generalized 2026-08-18 from a kbp4-only hardcode in SendSysEx.cpp's runAutomaticProcess() into this per-family field - same values, no behavior change for KBP4. Applied automatically by --fw-update to both the Peripheral and Central sends, regardless of --midi-backend; any of these still lose to an explicit -fcs/-fgd/-cd/-pd CLI flag.

Central's application-mode SysEx relay (and its bootloader's page-format parser) recognizes a valid message header within the first ~24 bytes and immediately starts a blocking operation on its end (consistent with an I2C flash-erase on the peripheral MCU it's relaying to, or the bootloader's own erase_app()) before it can accept more USB data. firstChunkSize=32 clears the host fast enough to avoid landing mid-blocking-op; firstGapDelayMs=3000 then gives the device several seconds' grace before the next window, after which it drains the rest of the transfer at chunkDelayMs=150. postDelayMs=3000 gives the bootloader/relay extra time to finish writing/verifying and reboot before the port closes. See firmware_1_2_2_0_central and firmware_1_2_2_0_peripheral's own notes below for the full hardware investigation and validated command history this was derived from (2026-08-13 through 08-17).
Requests a reboot into bootloader mode for K-Board Pro 4.
Superseded by firmware_1_2_2_0_central.
Superseded by firmware_1_2_2_0_peripheral.
targetState here is wrong (see firmware_1_2_2_0_peripheral note) - kept as bootloader only to match this superseded entry's original (also-wrong) filing; do not use.

No "role" field on this entry (unlike firmware_1_2_2_0_peripheral below) - deliberate: it keeps this the family's role-less/primary firmware target, which is what deviceDatabase::getPayloadPath("firmware", version) resolves by default (it now only matches role-less payloads unless a specific role is requested - see the schema's payloadAsset.role). This is what --fw-update KBP4's bootloader-flash step sends. Added 2026-08-15 after finding this entry and firmware_1_2_2_0_peripheral previously shared type="firmware"+version with both flagged default/latest and nothing to disambiguate them - getPayloadPath() was non-deterministic (took whichever matched entry appeared last in this array), which risked --fw-update KBP4 silently flashing the peripheral image into the Central bootloader.

Central firmware payload, current release candidate (Keil_release_dev, commit a03c344). Adds I2C_LOCK_BOOTLOADER: Central auto-locks its own and all 4 peripherals' bootloaders once it detects a fully-assembled 4-peripheral unit.

Single monolithic SysEx message (51913 bytes, exactly one F0...F7 pair) - a flat 512-byte-page flash image (PAGE_BEGINS/page_num/checksum/data), NOT Hex_to_SysEx's Intel-HEX-line-chunked format. The Central bootloader's payload parser only understands the page format; it cannot parse a Hex_to_SysEx-style multi-chunk file at all.

Do not send this as (or repackage it into) multiple independently-framed F0...F7 messages. packet_data_init() in the Central bootloader's MIDI_sysex.c calls erase_app() unconditionally on every validated message header with no once-per-transfer guard, so a second top-level SysEx message re-erases the entire app region and destroys whatever the first message just wrote. Only sendsysex's single-message sub-split path (-cs/-cd slicing the one F0...F7 message's bytes into smaller transport writes, inserting no new SysEx framing) is safe here - same mechanism already hardware-validated on BopPad. See k-board_pro_firmware's Firmware/_sysex_maker/BOOTLOADER_SYSEX_CAPABILITIES.md for the full investigation.

VALIDATED on real hardware 2026-08-13 (--midi-backend winmm): `SendSysEx -p <bootloader-port> -f v1.2.1.1_kbp4_central.syx -cs 32 -cd 100 -fgd 3000 --midi-backend winmm` completed in ~3 min (51913 bytes), device rebooted cleanly back to application mode afterward. See -fgd note on firmware_1_2_2_0_peripheral below for why this is needed under WinMM specifically - the same header-recognition-triggers-a-blocking-op behavior applies here (the bootloader's packet parser reacting to the recognized page header, not just the app-mode I2C relay path). -cs above 32 (tried 64, 512) fails outright even with -fgd, because the larger first window is still mid-transmission over USB when the device starts blocking, so the in-flight midiOutLongMsg call itself errors - has to be small enough to fully clear the host first. Plain WMS backend (no --midi-backend override) has not needed this workaround in testing so far; -fgd only matters when WinMM is forced.

FASTER, also validated on real hardware 2026-08-13: `SendSysEx -p <bootloader-port> -f v1.2.1.1_kbp4_central.syx -fcs 32 -cs 128 -cd 100 -fgd 3000 --midi-backend winmm` completed in ~50s (vs ~3min at a uniform -cs 32) - new -fcs/--first-chunk-size flag lets the first window stay small (32B, required to clear the host before the device's blocking op starts) while every window after it uses a larger -cs (128B validated; steady-state windows past the first gap tolerate more than the first one does). Device rebooted cleanly back to application mode afterward. This is the recommended command going forward.

This entry's own file (v1.2.2.0_kbp4_central.syx) was not the exact file physically sent above - the tested v1.2.1.1 file is byte-length-identical (51913 bytes) and shares the same page-format/header structure (same firmware pipeline, only the compiled app content differs), so the technique should carry over, but v1.2.2.0 itself has not yet been independently re-run through this exact command.

PREFERRED as of 2026-08-15 (user-designated), validated on real hardware: `SendSysEx -n "K-Board Pro 4 Bootloader 7" -f v1.2.1.1_kbp4_central.syx -fcs 32 -fgd 3000 -cs 512 -cd 100 -pd 3000 --midi-backend winmm` completed in ~16s. -pd 3000 (vs the 500ms default) gives the bootloader extra time to finish writing/verifying the final page and reboot cleanly before the port closes, on top of the -fcs 32/-fgd 3000 first-window handling.

CONFIRMED end-to-end on real hardware 2026-08-17: full `SendSysEx --fw-update KBP4` flow (Peripheral, then bootloader-entry, then this Central payload, then reboot) succeeds under both `--midi-backend winmm` and `--midi-backend wms`, fully automatic port discovery (no -p/-n needed). --fw-update KBP4 applies -fcs 32 -fgd 3000 -cd 150 -pd 3000 to both the Peripheral and Central sends automatically, regardless of backend - -cd bumped from 100 to 150 on 2026-08-16 (user-requested) for the automatic path specifically; manually-run raw-send commands above still used -cd 100 when validated. This also required two unrelated fixes surfaced by the first live --fw-update KBP4 run: (1) versionToString() was dropping the trailing ".0" of this entry's "1.2.2.0" version, so the default-version lookup failed before ever touching hardware - fixed by comparing parsed version_t structs instead of round-tripped strings (deviceDatabase.cpp); (2) WMS's port enumeration for the identity-request input port needed the named_application profile below (see its own note) to be found at all.

role="peripheral" (added 2026-08-15) excludes this entry from deviceDatabase::getPayloadPath("firmware", version)'s default role-less match, so --fw-update KBP4's generic bootloader-flash step (which always resolves the role-less payload) can never resolve to this one - see firmware_1_2_2_0_central's note for why that disambiguation was needed. Instead, kmiDevice::runAutomaticUpdate() looks this role up explicitly and sends it first, while Central is still in application mode, before triggering the bootloader-entry -> bootloader -> Central-firmware-flash -> reboot sequence (added 2026-08-15, matching the order the user validated manually below) - there is no independent version check against the device for this payload (peripherals have no MIDI identity of their own), so it is resent unconditionally whenever the Central version check decides an update is due. If --fw-update KBP4 is invoked while the device happens to already be sitting in Central's bootloader (e.g. resuming an interrupted prior run), this payload is sent as a catch-up step after Central's flash completes and the device reboots back to application mode, since it cannot be sent while Central is in bootloader mode.
Peripheral firmware payload, current release candidate (Keil_release_dev, commit a03c344).

targetState is application, not bootloader: the Peripheral bootloader has no SysEx/MIDI parser at all (no MIDI/ code in kbp4_peripheral_bootloader) and is only reachable over I2C. This payload must be sent to the Central APPLICATION port (message ID 0x2110/FIRMWARE_PERIPH_MESSAGE) while Central is running its normal app firmware, not the Central bootloader port. Central's app then puts all 4 peripherals into their own bootloaders over I2C, erases them, and relays this same page-formatted payload to each one as I2C_BLOCK_WRITE_FOLLOWS messages.
Same single-monolithic-message / page-format constraints as firmware_1_2_2_0_central apply here too - see that entry's notes and BOOTLOADER_SYSEX_CAPABILITIES.md.

VALIDATED on real hardware 2026-08-13 (--midi-backend winmm): `SendSysEx -p <application-port> -f v1.2.1.1_kbp4_peripheral.syx -cs 32 -cd 100 -fgd 3000 --midi-backend winmm` completed in ~2m15s (38353 bytes). Root cause of the plain -cs/-cd approach failing under WinMM: as soon as the Central app's SysEx relay recognizes the FIRMWARE_PERIPH_MESSAGE header (~first 24 bytes), it starts a blocking operation on its end (consistent with an I2C flash-erase kicked off on the peripheral before the transfer body arrives) and can't service the USB endpoint again for ~2-3 seconds. WinMM's midiOutLongMsg has no tolerance for that stall and surfaces it as a hard send error (WMS apparently queues/retries through it transparently, which is why this was never seen without --midi-backend winmm forced). -cs must stay small (32B validated; 64B and 512B both fail even with -fgd, because a bigger first window is still transmitting over USB when the device starts blocking, so that same in-flight send call fails) and sendsysex's new -fgd flag (--first-gap-delay) inserts one long settle delay after just the first window, then reverts to normal -cd speed for the rest of the transfer - confirmed the fast path holds for all ~1200 remaining 32-byte windows once past that first gap. It is safe to re-send this payload repeatedly if a transfer is interrupted; the Central relay re-erases the peripheral's flash on every attempt.

FASTER, also validated on real hardware 2026-08-13: `SendSysEx -p <application-port> -f v1.2.1.1_kbp4_peripheral.syx -fcs 32 -cs 128 -cd 100 -fgd 3000 --midi-backend winmm` completed in ~42s (vs ~2m15s at a uniform -cs 32) - new -fcs/--first-chunk-size flag lets the first window stay small (32B, required to clear the host before the device's blocking op starts) while every window after it uses a larger -cs (128B validated; steady-state windows past the first gap tolerate more than the first one does). This is the recommended command going forward.

Re-sending after an interrupted attempt requires re-entering the correct state per attempt: this payload's targetState is application, so the Central device must be back in its normal application-mode port (not a bootloader port) before retrying.

PREFERRED as of 2026-08-15 (user-designated), same command shape as firmware_1_2_2_0_central: `SendSysEx -n "K-Board Pro 4 7" -f v1.2.1.1_kbp4_peripheral.syx -fcs 32 -fgd 3000 -cs 512 -cd 100 -pd 3000 --midi-backend winmm` completed in ~18s on real hardware.

CONFIRMED end-to-end on real hardware 2026-08-17: `SendSysEx --fw-update KBP4` now sends this payload automatically (see the role="peripheral" note above for the orchestration), verified working under both `--midi-backend winmm` and `--midi-backend wms`. -cd bumped from 100 to 150 on 2026-08-16 (user-requested) for the automatic path specifically.

This entry's own file (v1.2.2.0_kbp4_peripheral.syx) was not the exact file physically sent above - the tested v1.2.1.1 file is byte-length-identical (38353 bytes) and shares the same page-format/header structure (same firmware pipeline, only the compiled app content differs), so the technique should carry over, but v1.2.2.0 itself has not yet been independently re-run through this exact command.
Matches WinMM's port naming (device enumerates as a single "K-Board Pro 4" port pair). See the named_application profile below for WMS's split-endpoint naming of the same physical device.

Matches WMS's port naming ("K-Board Pro 4 Control Surface" / "K-Board Pro 4 Expander") - added 2026-08-16 after --fw-update KBP4 under --midi-backend wms failed to find the device at all, since only the plain single_port name was registered. role "main" (shared with the WinMM application profile above, and with safeProbeRoles.application) so automatic-update port selection works identically regardless of which backend's naming actually matched. Mirrors qunexus.json's legacy_unnamed_application/named_application split exactly.
